questions.question:
11 is related to 45 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 3 is related to 13. To which of the following is 6 related following the same logic?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: 1st number × 4 +1 = 2nd number.**

11 is related to 45 

→ 11 × 4 +1

→ 44 + 1

→ 45

3 is related to 13

→ 3 × 4 +1

→ 12 + 1

→ 13 = 2nd number.

Similarly,

6 is related to

→ 6 × 4 +1

→ 24 + 1

**→ 25 **

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

 T is not an immediate neighbour of R. D is not an immediate neighbour of G.

Thus, T and G sit immediate left and to the immediate right of F.

questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

30 – 10 ÷ 63 × 9 + 15 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation: 30 – 10 ÷ 63 × 9 + 15 = ? 

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 30 + 10 × 63 ÷ 9 – 15 = ? 

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 30 + __**10 ×** **7**__ – 15 = ? 

⇒ 30 + __**70**__ – 15 = ? 

⇒ __**100 – 15**__ = ? 

⇒ __**85**__.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(11, 19, 8)

(14, 29, 15)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: 

Logic: 1st number + 3rd number = 2nd number.

Now,

For (11, 19, 8)

⇒ 11 + 8 = 19

For (14, 29, 15)

⇒ 14 + 15 = 29

For Option 1: (7, 35, 23)

⇒ 7 + 23 = 30 (Not matching)

For Option 2: (16, 28, 12)

⇒ 16 + 12

= 28 = 2nd number

For Option 3: (18, 21, 7)

⇒ 18 + 7 = 4 (Not matching)

For Option 4: (22, 25, 9)

⇒ 22 + 9 = 31 (Not matching)

Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.

Statements:

• Some glasses are cups.

• All cups are plates.

Conclusions:

(I) At least some plates are glasses.

(II) All cups are glasses.
questions.solution:

questions.question:
Which of the following interchanges of signs would make the given equation correct?

57 − 19 × 18 + 9 ÷ 45 = 18
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/c0j5U9v2oJWEzSTKvdDLWZ5Zik3PBUXk-C9w3Ma990WH63rpQUfA7g-3wh_uT7CgFvFJ4jPGEeOw509FxSgfh78_HR9tDNZ9KitXdEveKsLaLMgPQf6YSDt1b775728JMVp9FIQs=s0] 

Given equation: 57 − 19 × 18 + 9 ÷ 45 = 18

**1) Interchanging ÷ and −**

New equation: 57 ÷ 19 × 18 + 9 − 45 = 18

__**57 ÷ 19**__ × 18 + 9 − 45 = 18

__**3**__ __**× 18**__ + 9 − 45 = 18

__**54**__ + 9 − 45 = 18

63 − 45 = 18

18 = 18 (Correct)

**2) Interchanging ÷ and ×**

New equation: 57 − 19 ÷ 18 + 9 × 45 = 18

57 − __**19 ÷ 18**__ + __**9 × 45**__ = 18

57 − 1.05 + 405 ≠ 18 (Incorrect)

**3) Interchanging + and ÷**

New equation: 57 − 19 × 18 ÷ 9 + 45 = 18

57 − 19 × __**18 ÷ 9**__ + 45 = 18

57 − __**19 × 2**__ + 45 = 18

57 − 38 + 45 = 18

19 + 45 = 18

64 ≠ 18 (Incorrect)

**4) Interchanging + and ×**

New equation: 57 − 19 + 18 × 9 ÷ 45 = 18

57 − 19 + __**18 × 9**__ ÷ 45 = 18

57 − 19 + __**162 ÷ 45**__ = 18

57 − 19 + 3.6 ≠ 18 (Incorrect)

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
